desc: which terminal is on the console

name: console_rows

name: sys_cpu_load_pct
notes: percent of the task period

name: sys_jitter_pct
notes: percent of the task period

name: sys_stack_pct
notes: percent of the stack in use

name: sys_startup_sec
notes: nothing runs a law on a field that has not answered yet; 0 runs from the first beat

name: sys_control
notes: off stops every law and drops what they were driving to its declared safe state; per-program is `programs stop` or `programs disable`

name: sys_shutdown_sec
desc: laws stopped before the ending, seconds
notes: the mirror of sys_startup_sec: time for the record to reach flash before a reset

name: sys_retain_sec
desc: how often retained values reach flash
notes: 0 leaves only `save` and the way down; wear vs loss

name: plc_parkTimeout_sec
desc: how long a program may take to park, seconds
notes: the cap on the STOP hold: a ram that has not finished travelling is dropped safe and the log names it

name: rtu_timeout_ms
desc: how long a slave has to answer
notes: the bus default; a device model may declare its own

name: rtu_retries
desc: immediate retries before a device is backed off
notes: each costs a full timeout on a device that is really gone

name: rtu_backoff_ms
desc: first backoff after a device fails its retries
notes: doubles per further failure, up to rtu_backoff_max_ms

name: rtu_backoff_max_ms
desc: longest a backed-off device waits between probes
notes: what decides whether one dead device costs the whole bus

name: rtu_write_min_ms
desc: shortest interval between writes to one block
notes: what stops a chattering demand monopolising the bus

name: rtu_rewrite_ms
desc: how often an output block is written anyway
notes: MATCH the slave's own failsafe timer; it is watching for this
